name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_COMPREHENSION_Q65 - Formation of molecular orbitals in dioxygen

questiontext.text:
Passage: Molecular orbitals are formed by the overlap of atomic orbitals. Two atomic orbitals combine to form two molecular orbitals called bonding molecular orbital (BMO) and anti bonding molecular orbital (ABMO). Energy of anti bonding orbital is raised above the parent atomic orbitals that have combined and the energy of the bonding orbital is lowered than the parent atomic orbitals. Energies of various molecular orbitals for elements hydrogen to nitrogen increase in the order : \(\sigma 1s < \sigma^* 1s < \sigma 2s < \sigma^* 2s < (\pi 2p_x \simeq \pi 2p_y) < \sigma 2p_z < (\pi^* 2p_x \simeq \pi^* 2p_y) < \sigma^* 2p_z\) and for oxygen and fluorine order of energy of molecular orbitals is given below : \(\sigma 1s < \sigma^* 1s < \sigma 2s < \sigma^* 2s < \sigma 2p_z < (\pi 2p_x \simeq \pi 2p_y) < (\pi^* 2p_x \simeq \pi^* 2p_y) < \sigma^* 2p_z\). Different atomic orbitals of one atom combine with those atomic orbitals of the second atom which have comparable energies and proper orientation. Further, if the overlapping is head on, the molecular orbital is called 'Sigma' (\(\sigma\)) and if the overlap is lateral, the molecular orbital is called 'pi' (\(\pi\)). The molecular orbitals are filled with electrons according to the same rules as followed for filling of atomic orbitals. However, the order for filling is not the same for all molecules or their ions. Bond order is one of the most important parameters to compare the strength of bonds.

65. Which of the following statements is correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
According to Molecular Orbital Theory, the total number of molecular orbitals formed is always equal to the total number of combining atomic orbitals, and half of these are bonding molecular orbitals while the other half are antibonding molecular orbitals.

Step 2: Evaluation of Statements
Each oxygen atom has 5 atomic orbitals (\(1s, 2s, 2p_x, 2p_y, 2p_z\)) involved in forming \(\mathrm{O}_2\). Combining \(5 + 5 = 10\) atomic orbitals produces 10 molecular orbitals (5 bonding and 5 antibonding).
In \(\mathrm{O}_2\) (16 electrons), the \(\pi^* 2p_x\) and \(\pi^* 2p_y\) orbitals are half-filled and \(\sigma^* 2p_z\) is empty, so not all molecular orbitals are completely filled.
The total number of bonding molecular orbitals (5) is equal to the total number of antibonding molecular orbitals (5).
There are 5 filled bonding orbitals (10 electrons) and 3 occupied antibonding orbitals (6 electrons), so the numbers of filled bonding and antibonding orbitals are not equal.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, the only correct statement is that in the formation of dioxygen from oxygen atoms, 10 molecular orbitals will be formed.

answer.text: In the formation of dioxygen from oxygen atoms 10 molecular orbitals will be formed.
All the molecular orbitals in the dioxygen will be completely filled.
Total number of bonding molecular orbitals will not be same as total number of anti bonding orbitals in dioxygen.
Number of filled bonding orbitals will be same as number of filled anti bonding orbitals.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_COMPREHENSION_Q66 - Molecular orbital with maximum nodal planes

questiontext.text:
Passage: Molecular orbitals are formed by the overlap of atomic orbitals. Different atomic orbitals of one atom combine with those atomic orbitals of the second atom which have comparable energies and proper orientation. Further, if the overlapping is head on, the molecular orbital is called 'Sigma' (\(\sigma\)) and if the overlap is lateral, the molecular orbital is called 'pi' (\(\pi\)). 66. Which of the following molecular orbitals has maximum number of nodal planes?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A nodal plane (or nodal surface) is a plane where the electron wave function \(\psi\) changes sign and the probability density \(\psi^2\) is zero. Antibonding molecular orbitals possess an additional nodal plane perpendicular to the internuclear axis between the two nuclei, in addition to the nodal planes inherent to the combining atomic orbitals.

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Molecular Orbital
\(\sigma^* 1s\) is formed from two \(1s\) orbitals (0 atomic nodal planes each) combining out of phase, giving 1 nodal plane between the nuclei.
\(\pi 2p_x\) is formed from two \(2p_x\) orbitals combining in phase, giving 1 nodal plane containing the internuclear axis.
\(\pi^* 2p_y\) is formed from two \(2p_y\) orbitals combining out of phase, giving 2 nodal planes (one containing the internuclear axis and one perpendicular to it between the nuclei).
\(\sigma^* 2p_z\) is formed from two \(2p_z\) orbitals combining out of phase along the \(z\)-axis; it retains the two nodal planes passing through each nucleus (from the two \(2p_z\) orbitals) plus the central antibonding nodal plane between the nuclei, giving 3 nodal planes in total.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, \(\sigma^* 2p_z\) has the maximum number of nodal planes (3).

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_COMPREHENSION_Q67 - Pair of species having the same bond order

questiontext.text:
Passage: Molecular orbitals are formed by the overlap of atomic orbitals. Two atomic orbitals combine to form two molecular orbitals called bonding molecular orbital (BMO) and anti bonding molecular orbital (ABMO). Energy of anti bonding orbital is raised above the parent atomic orbitals that have combined and the energy of the bonding orbital is lowered than the parent atomic orbitals. Energies of various molecular orbitals for elements hydrogen to nitrogen increase in the order : \(\sigma 1s < \sigma^* 1s < \sigma 2s < \sigma^* 2s < (\pi 2p_x \simeq \pi 2p_y) < \sigma 2p_z < (\pi^* 2p_x \simeq \pi^* 2p_y) < \sigma^* 2p_z\) and for oxygen and fluorine order of energy of molecular orbitals is given below : \(\sigma 1s < \sigma^* 1s < \sigma 2s < \sigma^* 2s < \sigma 2p_z < (\pi 2p_x \simeq \pi 2p_y) < (\pi^* 2p_x \simeq \pi^* 2p_y) < \sigma^* 2p_z\). Different atomic orbitals of one atom combine with those atomic orbitals of the second atom which have comparable energies and proper orientation. Further, if the overlapping is head on, the molecular orbital is called 'Sigma' (\(\sigma\)) and if the overlap is lateral, the molecular orbital is called 'pi' (\(\pi\)). The molecular orbitals are filled with electrons according to the same rules as followed for filling of atomic orbitals. However, the order for filling is not the same for all molecules or their ions. Bond order is one of the most important parameters to compare the strength of bonds.

67. Which of the following pair is expected to have the same bond order?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
We need to compare the bond orders of the pairs: \(\mathrm{O}_2, \mathrm{N}_2\); \(\mathrm{O}_2^+, \mathrm{N}_2^-\); \(\mathrm{O}_2^-, \mathrm{N}_2^+\); and \(\mathrm{O}_2^-, \mathrm{N}_2^-\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Isoelectronic diatomic species have the same total number of electrons and therefore the same bond order.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
\[\text{Bond Order} = \frac{1}{2}(N_b - N_a)\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
For \(\mathrm{O}_2\) (16 electrons): \(\text{BO} = 2.0\); for \(\mathrm{N}_2\) (14 electrons): \(\text{BO} = 3.0\) (different).
For \(\mathrm{O}_2^+\) (\(16 - 1 = 15\) electrons): \(N_b = 10, N_a = 5 \implies \text{BO} = \frac{10 - 5}{2} = 2.5\).
For \(\mathrm{N}_2^-\) (\(14 + 1 = 15\) electrons): \(N_b = 10, N_a = 5 \implies \text{BO} = \frac{10 - 5}{2} = 2.5\).
For \(\mathrm{O}_2^-\) (17 electrons): \(\text{BO} = 1.5\); for \(\mathrm{N}_2^+\) (13 electrons): \(\text{BO} = 2.5\) (different).

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Both \(\mathrm{O}_2^+\) and \(\mathrm{N}_2^-\) have 15 electrons and a bond order of \(2.5\), so they are expected to have the same bond order.

name.text: NCERTEXEMPLAR_CHEMISTRY_UNIT4_COMPREHENSION_Q68 - Molecule where sigma 2pz is filled after pi 2px and pi 2py

questiontext.text:

Energies of various molecular orbitals for elements hydrogen to nitrogen increase in the order : \(\sigma 1s < \sigma^* 1s < \sigma 2s < \sigma^* 2s < (\pi 2p_x \simeq \pi 2p_y) < \sigma 2p_z < (\pi^* 2p_x \simeq \pi^* 2p_y) < \sigma^* 2p_z\) and for oxygen and fluorine order of energy of molecular orbitals is given below : \(\sigma 1s < \sigma^* 1s < \sigma 2s < \sigma^* 2s < \sigma 2p_z < (\pi 2p_x \simeq \pi 2p_y) < (\pi^* 2p_x \simeq \pi^* 2p_y) < \sigma^* 2p_z\). Different atomic orbitals of one atom combine with those atomic orbitals of the second atom which have comparable energies and proper orientation. Further, if the overlapping is head on, the molecular orbital is called 'Sigma' (\(\sigma\)) and if the overlap is lateral, the molecular orbital is called 'pi' (\(\pi\)). 68. In which of the following molecules, \(\sigma 2p_z\) molecular orbital is filled after \(\pi 2p_x\) and \(\pi 2p_y\) molecular orbitals?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
According to Molecular Orbital Theory, for homonuclear diatomic molecules from \(\mathrm{H}_2\) up to \(\mathrm{N}_2\), \(s\text{–}p\) mixing causes the \(\sigma 2p_z\) orbital to have higher energy than the degenerate \(\pi 2p_x\) and \(\pi 2p_y\) orbitals. By the Aufbau principle, lower-energy orbitals are filled first.

Step 2: Evaluation
For \(\mathrm{O}_2\), \(\mathrm{F}_2\), and \(\mathrm{Ne}_2\), the energy of \(\sigma 2p_z\) is lower than that of \(\pi 2p_x\) and \(\pi 2p_y\), so \(\sigma 2p_z\) is filled before them. For \(\mathrm{N}_2\), \((\pi 2p_x \simeq \pi 2p_y)\) is lower in energy than \(\sigma 2p_z\), so \(\sigma 2p_z\) is filled after \(\pi 2p_x\) and \(\pi 2p_y\).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Therefore, \(\sigma 2p_z\) is filled after \(\pi 2p_x\) and \(\pi 2p_y\) in \(\mathrm{N}_2\).
